note: How each school answers the core questions of ʿaqīda.

groups.origin: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal and the ḥadīth scholars; later Ibn Taymiyya
groups.where: Ḥanbalī circles historically; the Salafī movement today
texts: العقيدة الطحاوية (with Ibn Abī al-ʿIzz’s commentary)
groups.self: Followers of the Salaf: the Companions and the first generations. Belief is taken from the Qur’an and authentic Sunna as they understood it, not from kalām.
beliefs: Attributes are affirmed as stated, “without how” (بلا كيف), without likening them to creation or emptying them of meaning.
Faith is belief, word and deed, and rises and falls.
Kalām methods (proofs from accidents and bodies) are a blameworthy innovation.

sifat: Affirm every attribute in the texts with its apparent meaning, how it is unknown (الكيف مجهول); reject both likening and figurative interpretation.
qadar: Allah creates all acts; humans have a real will and power that truly affect their acts, by which they are accountable.
iman: Belief of the heart, statement of the tongue, action of the limbs; increases with obedience, decreases with sin.
kabira: A believer with deficient faith, not a disbeliever; in the hereafter under Allah’s will, not in Hell forever.
aql: Sound reason never truly conflicts with authentic revelation; where they seem to, revelation leads.
ruya: Believers will see Allah in the hereafter.
quran: Allah’s uncreated speech, spoken with letters and sound as He wills.
imama: By choice and allegiance (بيعة), not by designated text; the four caliphs rightly guided, in order of merit Abu Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthman, ʿAli.
sahaba: All are upright (عدول); silence over their disputes, which were ijtihād.
takfir: No takfīr of the people of the qibla for sins; only for clear disbelief, with conditions met and impediments removed.

groups.origin: Abū al-Ḥasan al-Ashʿarī (d. 324/936), Baghdad; systematised by al-Bāqillānī, al-Juwaynī, al-Ghazālī, al-Rāzī
groups.where: North and West Africa, Egypt (al-Azhar), the Levant, Yemen, South-East Asia; most Mālikīs and Shāfiʿīs
groups.self: Ahl al-Sunna wa al-Jamāʿa: defending the creed of the Salaf with rational proof against the Muʿtazila and the philosophers.
beliefs: Allah has eternal attributes of meaning (المعاني): power, will, knowledge, life, hearing, sight, speech.
Allah creates every act; the human “acquires” it (الكسب).
Good and bad, as grounds of reward and punishment, are known only by revelation.

sifat: Affirm the attributes of meaning; texts suggesting body or direction (hand, istiwāʾ) are either consigned to Allah (تفويض, earlier view) or interpreted fittingly (تأويل, later view).
qadar: Allah creates the act and the power with it; the human acquires the act (كسب); created power has no independent effect.
iman: Faith is assent of the heart (تصديق); speech is a condition for worldly rulings; deeds complete it. Many accept it rises and falls.
kabira: A believer with deficient faith, not a disbeliever; in the hereafter under Allah’s will, not in Hell forever.
aql: Reason proves Allah’s existence and prophethood; text that clashes with decisive reason is interpreted. Moral value is known by revelation only.
ruya: Believers will see Allah, without direction or likeness.
quran: Allah’s speech is an eternal attribute without letters or sound (الكلام النفسي); the recited and written words are created expressions of it.
imama: By choice and allegiance (بيعة), not by designated text; the four caliphs rightly guided, in order of merit Abu Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthman, ʿAli.
sahaba: All are upright (عدول); silence over their disputes, which were ijtihād.
takfir: No takfīr of the people of the qibla for sins; only for clear disbelief, with conditions met and impediments removed.

groups.where: The Ḥanafī world: Turkey, Central and South Asia, the Balkans
groups.self: Ahl al-Sunna wa al-Jamāʿa, continuing Abū Ḥanīfa’s creed (الفقه الأكبر) with rational proof.
beliefs: Like the Ashʿarīs on most points; adds bringing-into-being (التكوين) as an eternal attribute.
Reason can know Allah and basic good and evil even before revelation.
Faith is assent and does not rise or fall in itself.

sifat: Affirm the attributes of meaning plus التكوين; texts suggesting body are consigned or interpreted.
qadar: Allah creates the act; the human chooses it (اختيار) with real power, a larger role for choice than Ashʿarī kasb.
iman: Assent of the heart (with the tongue, for many); deeds are outside faith; faith itself neither rises nor falls.
kabira: A believer with deficient faith, not a disbeliever; in the hereafter under Allah’s will, not in Hell forever.
aql: Reason knows good and evil and the duty to know Allah even without a prophet (the Bukhārans held the duty comes with revelation).
ruya: Believers will see Allah, without direction or likeness.
quran: Eternal speech without letters or sound; the recited words are created.
imama: By choice and allegiance (بيعة), not by designated text; the four caliphs rightly guided, in order of merit Abu Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthman, ʿAli.
sahaba: All are upright (عدول); silence over their disputes, which were ijtihād.
takfir: No takfīr of the people of the qibla for sins; only for clear disbelief, with conditions met and impediments removed.

groups.origin: Wāṣil ibn ʿAṭāʾ (d. 131/748), Basra; peak under al-Maʾmūn; al-Qāḍī ʿAbd al-Jabbār
groups.where: No living school as such; its theology survives in Zaydī and Imāmī kalām and among modern rationalists
groups.self: The People of Justice and Oneness (أهل العدل والتوحيد), built on five principles: oneness, justice, the promise and threat, the intermediate position, commanding right and forbidding wrong.
beliefs: Allah’s attributes are not entities beside His essence.
Allah is just: He does not create sin and then punish it, so humans create their own acts.
The unrepentant grave sinner is neither believer nor disbeliever, and stays in Hell.

sifat: No eternal attributes beside the essence: Allah knows and acts by His essence; anthropomorphic texts are interpreted.
qadar: Humans create their own acts; otherwise punishing them would be unjust.
iman: Belief, word and deed; obligatory deeds are part of faith.
kabira: Neither believer nor disbeliever (المنزلة بين المنزلتين); in Hell forever if unrepentant.
aql: Reason comes first: it knows good, evil and obligation; texts are read in its light.
ruya: Allah will not be seen, since sight needs direction and body.
quran: Created speech that Allah brings into being.
imama: By election; they differed over the order of merit among the four caliphs.
sahaba: Upright in general, but those who fought ʿAli are judged by their deeds.
takfir: No takfīr for grave sins: the sinner is placed in the intermediate position instead.

groups.where: Extinct as a group; the name later used loosely for anyone denying attributes
texts: No surviving works of its own; known from الرد على الجهمية لأحمد والدارمي and heresiographies
beliefs: Allah is described by no attribute shared with creation.
Humans are compelled; acts are theirs only figuratively.
Paradise and Hell will come to an end.
groups.note: Known only through opponents’ reports, so every position here is as reported, not self-stated.

sifat: Denied the names and attributes (as reported).
qadar: Pure compulsion (جبر): humans have no power or choice.
iman: Faith is knowing Allah in the heart.
kabira: Sin does not remove faith, since faith is knowledge.
aql: Reason first; texts interpreted to fit it.

groups.origin: Kūfa; Ḥammād ibn Abī Sulaymān among early figures
groups.where: Not a living group; the faith-question survives as a Ḥanafī/Māturīdī position (“Murjiʾat al-fuqahāʾ”)
texts: No single creed text; views recorded in مقالات الإسلاميين للأشعري
groups.self: Those who “postpone” judgment of believers’ sins to Allah.
beliefs: Deeds are not part of faith.
Judgment of sinners is left to Allah.
Extreme strands said no sin harms a person who has faith.
groups.note: Two strands: the jurists, whose only difference was whether deeds are part of faith, and extremists who held sin harmless. Mainstream scholars treat them very differently.

iman: Assent (and, for many, statement); deeds are outside faith.
kabira: A believer; his fate is postponed to Allah.
sahaba: Withheld judgment on ʿUthman and ʿAli in their dispute.

groups.origin: Those who left ʿAli’s camp after the arbitration at Ṣiffīn; Azāriqa, Najdāt, Ṣufriyya
groups.where: Extinct as such; the Ibāḍīs, often grouped with them, reject the label (see Ibāḍī)
texts: No canonical text; letters and poetry, and heresiographies
groups.self: Those who “sold their souls to Allah” (الشراة); “judgment belongs to Allah alone” (لا حكم إلا لله).
beliefs: A grave sin takes a person out of faith.
Any upright Muslim may be caliph, and an unjust one must be removed.
Rejected the arbitration and those who accepted it.

iman: Belief, word and deed; leaving a duty breaks faith.
kabira: The grave sinner is a disbeliever; the Azāriqa held him an apostate to be fought.
imama: Any upright Muslim, not necessarily from Quraysh; removable for wrongdoing.
sahaba: Accept Abu Bakr and ʿUmar; reject ʿUthman’s later years, ʿAli after the arbitration, and the parties of the Camel and Ṣiffīn.
takfir: Takfīr for grave sins; extreme strands of all other Muslims.

groups.origin: Jābir ibn Zayd (d. c. 93/711) and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ibāḍ, Basra
groups.where: Oman, Zanzibar, the Mzab (Algeria), Jerba (Tunisia), Jabal Nafūsa (Libya)
groups.self: The People of Truth and Uprightness (أهل الحق والاستقامة); they reject being called Khawārij.
beliefs: Attributes are Allah’s essence itself.
The unrepentant grave sinner is ungrateful (كافر نعمة), not a polytheist.
Other Muslims are people of the qibla: marriage, inheritance and prayer with them are valid.

sifat: Attributes are the essence itself; texts implying likeness are interpreted.
qadar: Allah creates acts; humans acquire them.
kabira: “Kufr niʿma” (ingratitude), not polytheism; still a Muslim in worldly rulings; in Hell forever if unrepentant.
aql: Reason used to interpret texts that imply likeness.
imama: Elected from any upright Muslim, not necessarily Quraysh; may be latent (كتمان) in hard times.
sahaba: Honour Abu Bakr and ʿUmar; critical of ʿUthman’s later years and of ʿAli after the arbitration.
takfir: Other Muslims are not polytheists and not outside Islam.

groups.origin: Zayd ibn ʿAli ibn al-Ḥusayn (d. 122/740), Kūfa
groups.self: Followers of Zayd and of the imams of the Prophet’s House who rose for justice.
beliefs: ʿAli was the most meritorious; the imamate belongs to Fāṭima’s descendants who are qualified and rise (الخروج).
In theology close to the Muʿtazila.
Most accept the caliphate of Abu Bakr and ʿUmar (the less meritorious may lead).

sifat: Attributes are the essence; likeness denied.
kabira: An intermediate position (فاسق), in Hell if unrepentant.
aql: Reason knows good and evil; texts read in its light.
imama: ʿAli, al-Ḥasan, al-Ḥusayn by designation (by description); after them any qualified Fāṭimid who calls to himself and rises.
sahaba: ʿAli most meritorious; most accept the first two caliphs; cursing them rejected.

groups.origin: The imams from ʿAli to Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq (d. 148/765) and on; al-Mufīd, al-Ṭūsī, al-Ḥillī
groups.where: Iran, Iraq, Bahrain, Lebanon, Azerbaijan, parts of the Gulf and South Asia
groups.self: Followers of the Prophet’s House (أهل البيت): the five roots are oneness, justice, prophethood, imamate and the return.
beliefs: Allah appointed twelve infallible imams, the last of whom, al-Mahdī, is in occultation.
Allah is just: humans act by real choice, “neither compulsion nor delegation”.
Reason knows good and evil; legal rulings come through the imams’ teaching.

sifat: Attributes of essence are the essence itself; likeness denied; texts interpreted.
qadar: “Neither compulsion nor delegation, but a matter between the two” (لا جبر ولا تفويض).
iman: Belief, word and deed; full faith (إيمان) includes accepting the imamate.
kabira: A believer with deficient faith, not a disbeliever; in the hereafter under Allah’s will, not in Hell forever.
aql: Reason knows good and evil (الحسن والقبح العقليان); a source beside revelation.
imama: By divine designation (نص) of twelve infallible imams from ʿAli to the awaited Mahdī.
sahaba: Judged one by one; many faulted for not following ʿAli’s designation.
takfir: Sunnis are Muslims (مسلمون); full “faith” requires the imamate.

groups.origin: Those following Ismāʿīl son of Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq; the Fāṭimids; later Nizārī and Mustaʿlī branches
groups.where: Nizārīs (Aga Khan) worldwide, Central and South Asia; Mustaʿlī Bohras in India and Yemen
groups.self: Followers of the living imam of the Prophet’s line, who guides to the inner meaning of revelation.
beliefs: Every outward rule (ظاهر) has an inner truth (باطن), taught by the imam.
Allah is beyond every attribute, even beyond negation.
Allegiance to the imam (الولاية) is the first pillar.

sifat: Absolute transcendence: Allah is beyond all attributes and beyond their denial.
iman: Seven pillars, led by allegiance (الولاية) to the imam.
aql: The outer text has an inner meaning; the imam is its authority.
imama: A continuing line of designated imams: Nizārīs follow a present imam (the Aga Khan); Mustaʿlīs a hidden imam represented by a dāʿī.
sahaba: As with the Imāmīs, judged by their stance toward ʿAli.
